dct_description_sm: Exposure to most organochlorines (OCs) produces a wide variety of immunotoxic effects in animals and humans. The development of the immune system in utero and during infancy is particularly sensitive to immunotoxic agents. The Inuit population of Nunavik is exposed to immunotoxic OCs mainly through the consumption of fish and marine mammal fat. The effect of prenatal exposure to selected OCs on the incidence of acute infections in Inuit infants was investigated. The main objective of this project was to examine the effects of prenatal and postnatal exposure to organochlorines (OCs) and mercury on the immune system of Inuit infants from birth to 12 months of age. The specific objectives include: 1) Assessment of the prenatal and postnatal exposure to OCs and mercury; 2) Measurement of some immunological parameters (humoral and cellular immunity); and 3) Determination of the incidence of infections.
dct_subject_sm: Social sciences, economics and policy -> Inuit population
dct_title_s: Effects of Prenatal Exposure to Organochlorines and Mercury on the Immune System of Inuit Infants
